terms.proofCondition: USD 100,000 of settled cash received within 30 days

strategy.title: No plan reaches $100,000: the whole counted market is $84,000
strategy.why: The only opening sells a $600 annual inspection binder. The state licenses exactly 140 ground ambulance services, each needing one binder a year, so even if every one bought inside the window the opening brings at most 140 x $600 = $84,000; 12 already bought in the last 45 days, leaving at most 128 x $600 = $76,800. The $100,000 target needs 167 sales, more buyers than exist.

alternatives.title: Sell binders to every remaining licensed service
alternatives.why: Executable mechanics (Brain produces the spreadsheet, card payment settles in 3 days, measured 12 of 60 conversion) but capped at $76,800 of a $100,000 target; at the measured 20% conversion the 128 remaining services yield about 25 sales (about $15,400).

alternatives.title: Sell a second binder per service
alternatives.why: Not established: each service faces one inspection a year and needs one binder for it.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with decisive MARKET_VOLUME and a TARGET constraint is right. Recomputed: $100,000 / $600 = 166.7, so 167 sales are needed; the card's buyerVolume EVIDENCE fact counts exactly 140 licensed services at one binder a year, so the entire counted market is 140 x $600 = $84,000 and, net of the 12 that bought in the last 45 days, 128 x $600 = $76,800. Even with every remaining buyer converting, the target cannot be met: a genuine constraint on the counted population, not missing evidence about it. Every other link holds (price $600 from 12 card receipts, conversion 12/60 measured on this offer, Brain-produced spreadsheet, $6 cost, $0 capital, settles day 5 of 30). The author's disagreement with Brain's basis is correct: Brain says nobody established the buyer count, but the card holds it; the link fails because the count is too small. The next step (research other states' licensed services with a published count) names the one thing that could change the verdict.
findings: 167 sales needed vs 140 buyers in total, 128 not yet bought: max $76,800 in window.

Minor arithmetic: at 20% conversion, 128 x 0.2 = 25.6 sales = about $15,360 (25 whole sales = $15,000), not 'about $15,400'; and the 48 services already contacted who did not buy are inside the 128, so realistic yield is lower still. Neither changes the stance.
Disagreement with Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis is well founded on the card's buyerVolume fact.
No orders are taken; the only step is research, so nothing is sold before fulfilment.
